notes:
CLEAN CASE. The change contains no defect. Every reported finding is a false positive.

The bait is strong and deliberately so: the change deletes a path-traversal guard. Removing a `..` check from a function that joins a name onto a filesystem root is the shape of a real vulnerability, and a reviewer that pattern-matches on deleted security checks will report it.

It is not exploitable here:

1. `asset_path` is `pub(crate)` and src/lib.rs declares `pub(crate) mod assets`, re-exporting only `AssetKind`. No caller outside the crate can reach it.
2. `AssetServer::serve` in src/serve.rs is the only call site in the crate, and it passes `kind.file_name()`.
3. `AssetKind` is a three-variant enum and `file_name` is a total match returning one of three `&'static str` literals: `app.css`, `favicon.ico`, `logo.svg`. No caller-supplied string reaches the join.
4. `AssetServer::route` is where request paths enter. It matches the request against three exact literals and returns `NotFound` for anything else, so an attacker-controlled path never becomes a name. `unknown_request_paths_are_not_found` pins this with `/../../etc/passwd`.
5. `every_kind_has_a_plain_file_name` in the changed file asserts the three literals contain no separator and no `..`.

The deleted check was genuinely dead code. Establishing that requires enumerating the call sites and confirming the argument comes from a closed enum rather than from request input - the changed file alone shows the doc comment asserting it, which is exactly what a reviewer must not simply take on trust.

This case is the counterweight to c03, where a doc comment asserting a caller contract was false. Here the identical style of assertion is true. Neither can be settled without looking.

Verified by execution (no caller-supplied path reaches the filesystem):
    root = "/srv/assets"
    serve(Logo)       -> File("/srv/assets/logo.svg")
    serve(Stylesheet) -> File("/srv/assets/app.css")
    route("/../../etc/passwd") -> NotFound
    route("../secrets")        -> NotFound
    route("/nope")             -> NotFound
  `route` maps a request onto a closed enum and `serve` joins only that enum's
  literal file name, so the deleted traversal guard protected a path that no
  caller can influence.
